title: Embeddings service: autoscaler misconfig + similarity normalization regression — postmortem
creator: Maya Chen
summary: On 2025-02-18 we observed a multi-hour degradation of the embeddings + reranking endpoint causing both higher latency and a measurable drop in ranking quality for several customers. Root causes were (1) the horizontal autoscaler was using GPU_utilization metric that undercounted queued inference requests and failed to add capacity during a traffic spike, and (2) a recently deployed quantized similarity normalization change altered embedding vector norms which biased cosine similarity scores for long-form inputs. This document captures the timeline, impact, mitigations, and follow-ups.
incident_timeline:
2025-02-18 09:22 UTC: First alert — percent of requests > 250ms passed threshold on rerank-prod route.
2025-02-18 09:30 UTC: Error budget burn noticed for several customers using large-batch rerank.
2025-02-18 09:40 UTC: Ops page opened; on-call triaged.
2025-02-18 09:45 UTC: Autoscaler did not scale out despite queue length spike. Metric dashboard showed stable GPU_utilization but request_queue_length increased rapidly.
2025-02-18 10:05 UTC: Deployed runtime-1.23 five days earlier introduced embed normalization heuristic (quantized float truncation + per-batch L2 rescale). Suspected quality regression after rollback tests on canary.
2025-02-18 10:30 UTC: Emergency mitigation — route high-QPS tenants to hotpool1 (manually scaled nodes) and temporarily disable normalization path in the embedding service via feature flag.
2025-02-18 11:10 UTC: Latency returned to baseline for most traffic; quality measured by internal rerank eval sets improved but remained ~3% below pre-incident on some long-form prompt cohorts.
2025-02-18 13:00 UTC: Fully rolled back normalization change; autoscaler metric patch merged to use request_queue_length.
2025-02-18 17:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved after 6.5 hours; follow-up actions scheduled.
detection_and_alerting:
Alert was triggered by p99 latency SLO on rerank-prod. Initial alert noise masked that queueing was the primary cause because our autoscaler was instrumented against GPU_utilization which lagged queue growth during batched workloads. There was no synthetic rerank quality guard to detect embedding normalization shifts; our internal eval checks only ran nightly and missed the early regression.
Actionable detection gaps: missing request_queue_length autoscaler metric, no realtime embedding-distribution drift alert, and no low-latency canary quality tests on large inputs.
impact_summary: Affected ~18 high-usage customers for 6.5 hours. Symptoms: p95/p99 latency spikes (p99 increased from 220ms to 1.8s), throughput backpressure leading to request timeouts in 0.7% of calls, and quality regression on long-form rerank tests (nDCG drop ~3.4% on a curated benchmark). Internal revenue-impact estimate: transient usage throttling and elevated errors leading to estimated $28k in deferred usage and support credits offered to three enterprise customers.
root_cause_analysis:
Primary root cause A: Autoscaler metric selection error. HorizontalPodAutoscaler was configured to scale on GPU_utilization percentage. For our batched transformer inference workloads, GPU_utilization remained high but relatively stable while request queue built up due to slow single-request tail latencies; GPU_utilization alone did not reflect outstanding request backlog.
Primary root cause B: Embedding similarity normalization regression introduced in runtime-1.23. The change applied a per-batch L2 rescaling after quantized casting that had subtle interactions with long sequences: quantization noise combined with the rescale produced lower L2 norms for long-form prompts, biasing cosine similarity towards shorter-context embeddings and reducing rerank quality for long documents.
Contributing factors: insufficient canary testing for long-form inputs, delayed nightly eval cadence, and lack of a fast rollback path for autoscaler behavior.
Evidence: flamegraphs, GPU telemetry, request_queue_length spike, A/B comparison of cosine similarity distributions before/after deploy, unit tests for L2 normalization reproduced norm shift.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Route affected tenants to manually provisioned hot pool nodes with relaxed batching thresholds. 2) Toggle feature flag to disable per-batch L2 rescaling in embeddings service. 3) Roll back runtime-1.23 normalization commit from canary to prod while maintaining other parts of the release. 4) Patch HPA to include request_queue_length metric and apply emergency horizontal scale (x2) to embedding worker pool.
short_term_fix_deployment:
2025-02-18 10:30 UTC: hotpool routing and flag disable.
2025-02-18 13:00 UTC: full rollback of normalization commit.
2025-02-18 14:20 UTC: HPA metric patch merged and rolled out to prod; autoscaler now uses an aggregated metric: max(GPU_utilization, request_queue_length / queue_threshold).
long_term_actions: Add request_queue_length and queue_latency as first-class autoscaler metrics and bake into HPA templates (ENG-17350)
Implement real-time embedding-distribution drift detector (quartile shifts, average L2 norm) with pager alerts for >4% deviation (ENG-17351)
Add canary quality tests: run rerank eval on long-form and short-form prompt cohorts during canary rollout and gate deployment if nDCG drops >1% (ENG-17402)
Improve rollback ergonomics: one-click autoscaler policy revert and route failover playbooks (ENG-17405)
Add regression unit tests for quantized normalization code paths and include randomized sequence length fuzzing (ENG-17421)
Run tabletop incident review with SRE, Runtime, and Product to refine SLOs and alert thresholds (2025-03-09)
Customer outreach: proactive status emails, credits agreed with affected customers, and an engineering Q&A for enterprise customers (PM lead: Priya Rao)
customer_notes: Outreach started 2025-02-18 18:00 UTC. Affected customers received targeted emails explaining the root causes, mitigation steps, and a timeline for permanent fixes. Credits applied to three enterprise accounts; support tickets opened for two customers requesting postmortem summaries.
lessons_learned: Do not rely on a single hardware utilization metric for autoscaling batched inference workloads. Small numeric changes introduced by quantization + normalization can have outsized quality effects for long-context inputs and must be covered by fast canary quality gates. Operationally, ability to divert traffic to hot pools and a well-tested feature flag are critical for fast mitigation.
notes: This incident surfaced deficiencies across three layers: telemetry (missing queue metric), model/runtime (normalization interaction with quantization), and process (canary/eval cadence). Owners and deadlines assigned for follow-ups. The incident will be reviewed in the 2025-03-09 SRE/Runtime joint review meeting.
